Descripción de la compañía.

Ferrero es una empresa familiar con una perspectiva verdaderamente mundial y progresista y marcas icónicas como Nutella®, Tic Tac®, Ferrero Rocher®, Raffaello®, Kinder Bueno® y Kinder Sorpresa®. El amor por nuestras marcas sigue creciendo al igual que lo hace nuestro alcance internacional. Representada en más de 50 países y con productos vendidos en más de 170, el Grupo Ferrero encanta a numerosas generaciones en todo el planeta. ¿Cuál es el secreto de nuestro éxito mundial? 40,000 empleados especializados que celebran tanto el cuidado como la calidad para forjar un negocio, carreras profesionales y marcas de las que nos sentimos orgullosos. Únete a nosotros, podrías ser uno de ellos.

Nos encontramos en búsqueda de una persona responsable, comprometida, con ganas de aprender y desarrollarse en el área de Marketing. Nuestros Beneficios y ventajas:

Carreras con cuidado integrado: descubre nuestros beneficios aquí

Acerca de Ferrero:

Ferrero comenzó su trayectoria en la pequeña ciudad de Alba en Piamonte, Italia, en 1946. Hoy en día, es una de las empresas de alimentos dulces envasados más grandes del mundo, con muchas marcas icónicas que se venden en todo el mundo. Descubre más sobre Ferrero en ferrero.com.

¿Cómo ser exitoso en el rol y en Ferrero?

Consumidores, calidad y servicio son la clave de todo cuanto hacemos. Así pues, para cosechar el éxito en Ferrero, deberás orientarte al consumidor y al producto tanto como nosotros: dedicarte a lograr buenos resultados para los clientes en todo el mundo.

Ferrero se compromete a construir una cultura diversa e inclusiva donde todos los empleados se sientan bienvenidos, valorados y tengan las mismas oportunidades. Creemos que todos nuestros empleados tienen el mismo talento, cada uno a su manera. Al fomentar la curiosidad y las habilidades naturales de nuestros empleados, les proporcionamos, generación tras generación, los medios para alcanzar el éxito personal y profesional, permitiéndoles forjar su trayectoria en Ferrero. title: Head of Growth, Tilt Mexico
skills: Own the full growth funnel: Lead acquisition, activation, retention and cross-sell as one strategy, measured on profitable customers rather than installs or approvals. Paid acquisition stays the engine; you'll bring lifecycle and brand up to parity over time.

Drive performance marketing sophistication: Allocate the acquisition budget across channels with rigour: proper attribution, event-based optimisation, and payback and CAC (customer acquisition cost) discipline tied to credit outcomes. Push beyond the current channel mix into new paid, partnership, referral and app store channels, backed by steady creative testing.

Make growth and credit work together: Use the unit economics model with Credit and Data Science to decide which customers to acquire, at what cost and through which channels. Make sure growth targets account for approval rates and losses, not just volume.

Build the brand and its measurement: Define how Tilt shows up in Mexico, in voice, visual identity and awareness strategy, and put in place the measurement it lacks today: brand tracking, organic search and app store visibility, and social listening.

Grow customer value through lifecycle and cross-sell: Build triggered campaigns across push, SMS, WhatsApp, email and in-app that move customers from first loan to repeat loans, installment loans and the credit card. Partner with Product and Engineering to define what the lifecycle stack needs, and own the strategy that runs on it.

Run a small, leveraged team: Lead a tight, high-output team that uses AI for creative production, budget allocation and analytics rather than defaulting to headcount growth. Share what works with the growth teams in our other markets: the US, Brazil, India and the Philippines.
8+ years in growth or marketing, with hands-on performance marketing experience earlier in your career. You've personally run campaigns, not just overseen them.
You've had real budget accountability: your name on spend decisions, not just advisory input.
Consumer fintech or digital lending experience in Mexico or Latin America. You understand how acquisition cost, approval rates and credit losses shape what growth is worth.
Strong quantitative fluency. CAC, LTV (lifetime value), payback, attribution models and A/B test design (sample size, statistical significance) are second nature.
Familiarity with CRM and lifecycle tooling (Iterable or equivalent). You know what good looks like, even if you weren't the one building it.
You hold both halves of growth at once, analytical rigour and creative judgment, and you're honest about where your edge sits.
An AI-native mindset. You use agentic AI tools to raise your team's speed and quality, and you see AI as a force multiplier, not a threat to headcount.
Native or fluent Spanish and professional fluency in English.
Bonus: Hands-on experience with AppsFlyer (or a comparable mobile attribution platform) for install and event measurement.
Initial Recruiter Call: A conversation to learn about your experience and what you're looking for in your next role.
Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper discussion about your experience.
Skills Panel: Meet with Tilt team members to discuss your expertise and problem-solving approach.
Leadership Conversation: A final conversation with a leader to discuss how you'll contribute to Tilt's mission, and how we can help you achieve your career goals along the way.
Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

description:
Join the Tilt team

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.

The Opportunity: Head of Growth, Tilt Mexico

Mexico was Tilt's first market outside the US. Since 2022, our mobile-first personal loan has helped over 1 million customers access short-term credit on transparent, affordable terms. We now offer a 3-month installment loan and are rolling out a credit card in beta. As Head of Growth, you'll own how Tilt Mexico finds, activates and keeps customers across all three products, with real budget accountability and the mandate to drive profitable growth.

Acquisition works today but is concentrated in a few paid channels. Lifecycle and cross-sell are early, and the brand is under-measured. This is a chance to build an AI-native growth function in one of Latin America's largest and fastest-moving consumer credit markets.

This is a remote role based in Mexico. Travel for company onsites is expected at least four times a year.

How You'll Make An Impact


Own the full growth funnel: Lead acquisition, activation, retention and cross-sell as one strategy, measured on profitable customers rather than installs or approvals. Paid acquisition stays the engine; you'll bring lifecycle and brand up to parity over time.
Drive performance marketing sophistication: Allocate the acquisition budget across channels with rigour: proper attribution, event-based optimisation, and payback and CAC (customer acquisition cost) discipline tied to credit outcomes. Push beyond the current channel mix into new paid, partnership, referral and app store channels, backed by steady creative testing.
Make growth and credit work together: Use the unit economics model with Credit and Data Science to decide which customers to acquire, at what cost and through which channels. Make sure growth targets account for approval rates and losses, not just volume.
Build the brand and its measurement: Define how Tilt shows up in Mexico, in voice, visual identity and awareness strategy, and put in place the measurement it lacks today: brand tracking, organic search and app store visibility, and social listening.
Grow customer value through lifecycle and cross-sell: Build triggered campaigns across push, SMS, WhatsApp, email and in-app that move customers from first loan to repeat loans, installment loans and the credit card. Partner with Product and Engineering to define what the lifecycle stack needs, and own the strategy that runs on it.
Run a small, leveraged team: Lead a tight, high-output team that uses AI for creative production, budget allocation and analytics rather than defaulting to headcount growth. Share what works with the growth teams in our other markets: the US, Brazil, India and the Philippines.


Why you're a great fit


8+ years in growth or marketing, with hands-on performance marketing experience earlier in your career. You've personally run campaigns, not just overseen them.
You've had real budget accountability: your name on spend decisions, not just advisory input.
Consumer fintech or digital lending experience in Mexico or Latin America. You understand how acquisition cost, approval rates and credit losses shape what growth is worth.
Strong quantitative fluency. CAC, LTV (lifetime value), payback, attribution models and A/B test design (sample size, statistical significance) are second nature.
Familiarity with CRM and lifecycle tooling (Iterable or equivalent). You know what good looks like, even if you weren't the one building it.
You hold both halves of growth at once, analytical rigour and creative judgment, and you're honest about where your edge sits.
An AI-native mindset. You use agentic AI tools to raise your team's speed and quality, and you see AI as a force multiplier, not a threat to headcount.
Native or fluent Spanish and professional fluency in English.
Bonus: Hands-on experience with AppsFlyer (or a comparable mobile attribution platform) for install and event measurement.


Our Interview Process


Initial Recruiter Call: A conversation to learn about your experience and what you're looking for in your next role.
Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper discussion about your experience.
Skills Panel: Meet with Tilt team members to discuss your expertise and problem-solving approach.
Leadership Conversation: A final conversation with a leader to discuss how you'll contribute to Tilt's mission, and how we can help you achieve your career goals along the way.


Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Get At Tilt


Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.
Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.
Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.
Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.
Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)
Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.


The Tilt Way

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.

You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

skills: Setting the strategy: turning company and product strategy into clear positioning, segmentation, and go-to-market choices: where we play, who we serve, and how we win in Mexico.
Owning the story end to end: building one consistent narrative across the product ecosystem, including campaigns, owned channels, paid media, influencers, customer journeys, and support.
Shaping the roadmap early: partnering with Product and Research from the start so customer needs, barriers, and proof points drive what we build and how we talk about it.
Leading launches: running GTM for new products and updates, and aligning cross-functional teams on investment, audiences, channels, messaging, and success metrics.

Knowing the customer deeply: understanding the lifecycle, segments, and jobs-to-be-done, and working with Product and Growth to make every journey coherent, on-brand, and relevant to Mexican customers.
Reading the market: maintaining a sharp view of Mexico's competitive landscape and turning research, data, and competitive signals into clear calls on what we say, build, and test next.
Building the operating system: establishing rituals for narrative development, launch readiness, prioritization, measurement, and quarterly planning.
Cutting through ambiguity: bringing clarity and sound judgment to cross-functional problems, balancing strategic quality with speed.
Raising the bar: codifying best practices and creating reusable playbooks that level up Product Marketing.
Working AI-first: using AI for writing, research, analysis, and workflow automation, and continually finding ways to move faster and go deeper.
5–8+ years in product marketing or very similar roles at consumer tech or fintech companies, including time as a PMM on high‑impact launches.
Proven track record owning end‑to‑end product or major feature launches with clear, quantified business impact.
Strong customer-insight judgment: you can combine qualitative research, quantitative data, market signals, and frontline feedback into a clear point of view.
Hands-on experience using AI tools as a natural part of your day‑to‑day work.
Strategic GTM leadership: designing customer-led plans tailored to product tiering, with the operational excellence required to execute them effectively.
Experience across multiple areas (e.g., growth, brand, lifecycle, paid) and working with senior cross‑functional stakeholders.

Experience working with product-led growth, digital platforms, or mobile applications.

description:
About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

About The Role

We're hiring an experienced, curious Product Marketing Manager to shape how our products are positioned, launched and grown in Mexico. You'll use research, customer behavior and data to find barriers and opportunities, size their impact, and decide on audience, message, channels and investment. Building the operating system: establishing rituals for narrative development, launch readiness, prioritization, measurement, and quarterly planning.
Cutting through ambiguity: bringing clarity and sound judgment to cross-functional problems, balancing strategic quality with speed.
Raising the bar: codifying best practices and creating reusable playbooks that level up Product Marketing.
Working AI-first: using AI for writing, research, analysis, and workflow automation, and continually finding ways to move faster and go deeper.

All roles at JumpCloud® are Remote unless otherwise specified in the Job Description.


About JumpCloud®


JumpCloud® is the AI-powered unified IT management platform designed to secure the modern workforce. By consolidating identity, device, and access management, JumpCloud provides intelligent, secure IT that scales from human users to autonomous AI agents. We help organizations around the globe eliminate complexity and turn AI risk into an optimized advantage, ensuring the right people and agents have secure access to the right resources at all times.




 


JumpCloud is Intelligent, Secure IT.





About the Role: 


As a Product Marketing Manager, you will work directly under experienced Marketing leadership and alongside senior PMMs who set the strategic direction while giving you real ownership to build, ship, and see your work impact JumpCloud.




Responsibilties:






Build High-Impact Sales Plays & Enablement: Create practical pitch decks, competitive battlecards, demo scripts, and objection-handling guides that equip our global sales team to win more deals. 








Craft Buyer-Centric Messaging & Collateral: Translate complex Identity and Access Management (IAM), directory services, and cloud security capabilities into clear, compelling marketing assets for technical buyers. 








Deliver Actionable Competitive Intelligence: Research key competitors, map out JumpCloud’s differentiators, and turn market insights into takeaways the sales and marketing teams can use right away. 








Turn Short Briefs into Finished Work Fast: Partner with Marketing leadership, senior PMMs, sales, and product teams to take well-defined project briefs and deliver polished assets on tight timelines. 








Use AI to Move at High Velocity: Leverage modern AI productivity tools and workflows to speed up research, sharpen copy, and scale your output across GTM initiatives.












What We're Looking for: 






2–4 Years of B2B Experience: Background in B2B SaaS or tech across roles such as product marketing, sales enablement, content marketing, customer marketing, field/partner marketing, demand generation, or corporate communications—or customer-facing roles like Sales Engineer, SDR, or Customer Success Manager with standout writing skills. 








Crisp, Persuasive Writing: Proven ability to take technical concepts and distill them into clear, engaging copy that resonates with business and technical buyers. 








Rapid Learning Curve: Ability to quickly master a new product, buyer persona, and competitive landscape, even without a traditional PMM background. 








Strong Listening & Execution: You listen closely, ask smart questions up front, and turn a concise brief into the right deliverable the first time. 








High Bias for Action & Coachability: You turn work around quickly, welcome direct feedback without ego, iterate fast, and proactively look for the next task. 








Reliability & Creative Problem-Solving: You hit your deadlines, flag blockers early when they arise, and show up with proposed solutions rather than just questions. 








Bilingual Communication: Full professional fluency in English (for global GTM collaboration and asset creation) and Spanish.



















Where you’ll be working/Location:




JumpCloud® is committed to being Remote First, meaning that you are able to work remotely within the country noted in the Job Description.




 




This role is remote in the country of Mexico. You must be located in and authorized to work in Mexico to be considered for this role.  




 




Language: 




JumpCloud® has teams in 15+ countries around the world and conducts our internal business in English. The interview and any additional screening process will take place primarily in English. To be considered for a role at JumpCloud®, you will be required to speak and write in English fluently.  Any additional language requirements will be included in the details of the job description.




 




Why JumpCloud®? 




If you thrive working in a fast, SaaS-based environment and you are passionate about solving challenging technical problems, we look forward to hearing from you! JumpCloud® is an incredible place to share and grow your expertise! You’ll work with amazing talent across each department who are passionate about our mission. We’re out of the box thinkers, so your unique ideas and approaches for conceiving a product and/or feature will be welcome. You’ll have a voice in the organization as you work with a seasoned executive team, a supportive board and in a proven market that our customers are excited about.  




 




One of JumpCloud®'s three core values is to “Build Connections.” To us that means creating " human connection with each other regardless of our backgrounds, orientations, geographies, religions, languages, gender, race, etc. We care deeply about the people that we work with and want to see everyone succeed." - Rajat Bhargava, CEO




 




Please submit your résumé and brief explanation about yourself and why you would be a good fit for JumpCloud®.  Please note JumpCloud® is not accepting third party resumes at this time.   




 




JumpCloud® is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.




 




Scam Notice:

These scams may involve fake job postings, unsolicited emails, or messages claiming to be from our recruiters or hiring managers. Please note that JumpCloud will never ask for any personal account information, such as credit card details or bank account numbers, during the recruitment process. WE'RE HIRING: CITY PR HEAD – MEXICO CITY

Bureau of Architecture Media (BAM)

Location: Mexico City, Mexico

Work Mode: Remote

Role: City PR Head

Industry: Architecture, Design & Media




BAM is expanding into Latin America. We're looking for someone to lead our presence in Mexico City.

Bureau of Architecture Media (BAM) is a global architecture and design media platform connecting architecture practices, interior designers, editors, journalists, writers and creative professionals from across the world.

We are looking for a confident, well-connected and entrepreneurial communications professional to represent BAM in Mexico City and help us build a strong presence within Mexico's architecture and design ecosystem.

This is a remote opportunity, but not a desk-only role. It involves meeting studio principals, developing industry relationships, attending events, creating content and building BAM's local network.

As City PR Head, you will be the face of BAM in Mexico City — driving business development, developing media relationships, managing client engagements and building a community around architecture and design.




What you'll be responsible for

1. Business Development & Studio Relationships

Identify and connect with architecture and interior design practices across Mexico City.
Build relationships with studio founders, principals and decision-makers.
Introduce BAM's PR, communications and media services to prospective clients.
Develop new business opportunities and convert prospective studios into paying clients.
Manage existing client relationships, including regular in-person check-ins.

2. Media & Editorial Relationships

Build and maintain relationships with Mexican architecture and design editors, journalists and publications.
Identify relevant editorial opportunities for BAM clients.
Develop personalised pitches and project submissions for local publications.
Coordinate Spanish-language press materials, pitches and award submissions.
Connect Mexican practices with relevant international architecture and design media.

3. Content & Public Representation

Host and participate in interviews with architects and designers.
Appear in BAM's video content, reels, podcasts and project films.
Create short-form videos and event coverage.
Represent BAM at architecture and design exhibitions, launches, conferences and industry gatherings.

4. Community Building

Organise BAM meetups and networking initiatives in Mexico City.
Build connections with architects, designers, brands, editors and event organisers.
Develop local partnerships and represent BAM at relevant industry events.
Help establish BAM as an active participant in Mexico's architecture and design community.




Who should apply?

We're looking for someone who:

Has experience in PR, communications, media, marketing or business development.
Understands Mexico's architecture and interior design industry, particularly the Mexico City market.
Is fluent in Spanish and has strong English communication skills.
Has excellent networking and relationship-building abilities.

Picture yourself brightening someone’s day. When you join our Hotels team, that’s exactly what you’ll do every time you come to work! As a Director of Marketing  & Communications , you’re not just leading the development and execution of strategic marketing initiatives for the hotel – you’re spreading the light and warmth of hospitality by delivering memorable experiences that make the stay for every guest.

The Director of Marketing & Communications is responsible for developing and leading the integrated marketing, communications, public relations, digital, social media and brand strategy for Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal.

As a senior leader and steward of one of the world’s most distinctive luxury resorts, the Director will strengthen the resort’s positioning and desirability within the global luxury travel market while developing strategic initiatives that contribute to revenue, market share, reputation and long-term brand equity.

Working closely with Resort leadership, Sales, Revenue Management, Food & Beverage, Spa & Wellness, Events and Operations, the Director will ensure that all marketing and communications initiatives are strategically aligned, commercially relevant and consistent with Waldorf Astoria brand standards.

Develop and execute marketing strategies: Lead branding, messaging, and multi-channel marketing plans aligned with hotel goals, adjusting tactics based on market trends and performance data
Manage planning and operations: Oversee annual marketing budgets and coordinate resources for effective campaign deployment across traditional, digital, and social media platforms

At Hilton, Our Core Values Define What It Takes To Succeed Here And Guide The Qualities We Look For In Every Team Member

At Hilton, we don’t just deliver exceptional experiences for our guests—we build an exceptional workplace for the Team Members who make it all possible. As a global leader in hospitality, we’ve welcomed more than 3 billion guests worldwide, all while staying true to our founding vision: to fill the earth with the light and warmth of hospitality.

Our award-winning culture has earned us repeated recognition on the World’s Best Workplaces list by Great Place to Work and Fortune. Acerca de PayJoy




 




PayJoy, una Corporación de Beneficio Público, es una empresa de crédito con una misión clara: ayudar a clientes desatendidos en mercados emergentes a alcanzar la estabilidad y el éxito financiero. A través del financiamiento en punto de venta y y las ofertas de tarjetas de PayJoy, los clientes obtienen acceso a una vida moderna y de calidad. El crédito de PayJoy también les permite aprovechar oportunidades como microempresarios y actuar como una forma de seguro. Al aprovechar tecnologías avanzadas como el aprendizaje automático, la ciencia de datos y la inteligencia artificial para la prevención del fraude, hemos prestado servicio a más de 18 millones de clientes hasta 2025, logrando una sólida rentabilidad que impulsa un crecimiento sostenible.

El representante de soporte a clientes es responsable de atender a los aliados comerciales para atender y solucionar los problemas que tienen con los clientes finales a fin de retenerlos y hacer crecer el negocio.

Regional Aftersales Manager




We’re hiring a Regional Aftersales Manager to elevate our customer experience and strengthen our dealer network performance across the region.




In this role, you will act as the key connection between our corporate Aftersales leadership and the day‑to‑day operations of our dealerships. Your mission is to ensure that every customer receives a consistent, high‑quality service experience and that our aftersales operations continue to grow in efficiency, excellence, and profitability.




What You Will Be Responsible For




As a Regional Aftersales Manager, you will:




Implement standardized service processes across all regional dealerships to ensure alignment with global and OEM guidelines.
Monitor, analyze, and improve aftersales KPIs, including CSAT/NPS, Fixed First Visit rates, Service Retention, Workshop Absorption, and technical case performance.
Lead the resolution of high‑impact customer concerns and complex technical escalations, working closely with technical support teams and dealer principals.
Conduct regular dealer visits, field audits, and coaching sessions to strengthen service operations, improve workshop productivity, and elevate customer-handling standards.
Collaborate with the Aftersales Director to translate regional insights into strategic actions that support business growth, service marketing, parts performance, and customer retention initiatives.

What You Bring




Strong understanding of dealer operations, workshop management, parts processes, warranty, quality, and customer complaint resolution.
5–8 years of experience in automotive aftersales, field operations, or service engineering (OEM experience strongly preferred).
Proven results improving CSAT/NPS, FFV, retention, or dealer performance metrics.
Experience working with CRM systems, DMS platforms, dashboards, and reporting tools.
Advanced English communication skills and a customer‑centric mindset.
Exceptional analytical ability, organizational skills, and leadership presence when working with cross‑functional teams or dealer stakeholders.
A proactive, solutions‑oriented attitude, especially when managing escalations under time pressure.




Who Will Succeed in This Role




This position is ideal for someone who:




Is passionate about improving customer experience.
Enjoys solving complex problems with a strategic and data‑driven approach.
Can influence and guide dealer teams without direct authority.
Thrives in a dynamic, fast‑paced environment.
Understands that aftersales is not just a department — it’s a key driver of brand reputation and long‑term loyalty.

En Vemo somos un ecosistema integral de electromovilidad. Conectamos tecnología, infraestructura y personas para hacer posible una mejor forma de movernos.

Nos mueve hacer que más personas y empresas puedan dar el paso hacia la movilidad eléctrica. Todos los días integramos soluciones y acompañamiento para resolver los retos de esa transición, con las personas al centro de lo que construimos. Y queremos que seas parte.

Buscamos un Growth Analyst de Paid Media que convierta cada peso invertido en Meta y Google en resultados de negocio medibles, con foco en datos, medición y automatización. Debe tener mentalidad de negocio y ligar el rendimiento de medios con las etapas cruciales del funnel y las unidades de negocio, no con métricas de plataforma. ¿Cuál será tu misión?

Ser dueño/a del rendimiento de la inversión en medios pagados: decides dónde va el siguiente peso con base en el costo por etapa crucial del funnel y el retorno por línea de negocio, y construyes el sistema de medición que le da a Meta y Google señales de clientes reales, no de leads.

description:
Hello! 







At Factorial we're looking for a new Performance Marketing Manager for the Mexican market to help us support and scale our Paid Channels team to the next level. As part of the team in charge of driving customer acquisition and accelerating our growth, you'll be in charge of owning our paid acquisition strategy, experimenting with new growth opportunities, and working closely with Marketing and Sales to turn campaigns into qualified pipeline, new customers and recurring revenue.







Ready to be part of the challenge? 







About the Team 







Our Marketing team brings Factorial’s story to life, connecting our solutions with the businesses that need them most. We combine creativity, data, and experimentation to build impactful campaigns and drive sustainable growth across markets.







About the Role 







You’ll lead the strategy and execution of our paid acquisition channels in Mexico, reporting to our Global Expansion team and Paid Growth leadership. Your mission is to scale customer acquisition, improve marketing efficiency, and strengthen Factorial’s position in the Mexican market.







We’re looking for someone who goes beyond clicks and leads — someone who understands how performance marketing contributes to pipeline quality, customer acquisition, and long-term revenue growth.

About Factorial 







Founded in Barcelona in 2016, we now have +1,700 employees serving more than 16,000 companies across 112 countries.







Factorial started with a simple idea: companies were spending too much time managing processes and not enough time doing the work they were hired to do: their best work.







But as companies grow, work gets more disconnected. More people, more tools, more information, and more time spent connecting the dots. Generic AI can answer questions, but it doesn’t know your company. Every time, you have to give it the context.







Factorial is different. Because it’s inside the company, it already knows how it works, including its people, processes, policies, and data. So you can ask it to do real work, from screening candidates and managing expenses to answering questions and creating reports.







AI isn’t the goal. Giving people back their time is.







Factorial is the AI for Business that knows companies, connects how work happens across the business, and turns that context into action.

Our client is a U.S.-based performance marketing agency specializing in helping high-growth brands scale through data-driven digital advertising, creative strategy, and emerging commerce channels.

TikTok Shop Ads Specialist (GMV Max / Spark Ads) to lead performance and social commerce strategies for high-growth eCommerce brands.

The ideal candidate combines advanced paid media expertise with a deep understanding of how consumers discover and purchase products through TikTok. You should be comfortable managing significant advertising budgets, analyzing performance data, identifying winning creative quickly, and making real-time optimization decisions.

This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of performance marketing, social commerce, creative experimentation, and emerging technology.

You will have direct exposure to high-growth eCommerce brands and significant advertising budgets while helping shape TikTok Shop strategies in a fast-moving environment where creative thinking, analytical decision-making, and speed to market are critical.

Develop paid media strategies designed to increase TikTok Shop GMV while maintaining brand-specific profitability targets

Maintain a strong understanding of TikTok-native content and what drives users from discovery to purchase


Analytics & Reporting

TikTok Shop Affiliate Center

About WPP Media

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. For more information, visit wppmedia.com.

Role Summary And Impact

As part of the Global Operations Centre (GOC), you will work closely with teams across the United States, Europe, and Asia to deliver high-impact solutions in a collaborative, multicultural environment. We are looking for a Senior Associate, Digital Production, GOC who will:


End-to-End Campaign Delivery & Coordination Manage campaign workflows from brief interpretation to post-campaign analysis while leading status calls, managing timelines, and keeping deliverables aligned across teams.

Advanced level of English (this will be assessed during the interview process) 
Bachelor’s degree 
Proven understanding of digital media channels and campaign delivery fundamentals, with hands-on experience using ad-serving and trafficking platforms. 
Comfortable working with campaign data, building performance reports, and applying strong analytical skills to solve delivery challenges. 
Highly organized with sharp attention to detail, strong process management skills, and clear verbal and written communication. 


Life At WPP Media & Benefits

Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. We also Lead Optimistically, firmly believing in and Championing Growth and Development for every individual. This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising.

We Create an Open environment built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. This inclusive culture is fostered through a variety of employee resource groups and frequent in-office events showcasing team wins, sharing thought leadership, and celebrating holidays and milestone events. Our comprehensive benefits package reflects this commitment, including competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days.

WPP Media is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to characteristics. We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection in this open and supportive environment. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process. Please note that while our philosophy is the same across WPP, benefits may vary by office/country.

This position is available in a Remote or Hybrid Work Modality. The candidate must perform their work from any location within Mexico. Only Mexican nationals residing in the country or foreign nationals with a valid work permit may apply. Remote work from abroad is not permitted under any circumstances.

description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different


The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call


Requirements

What You'll Own


Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone


Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)


Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them


Who You Are

AI-native. You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer. You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp. Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation. You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel. You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient. Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority. PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.

This Role Is NOT

skills: The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call

Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read

The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment

The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone

description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different


The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call


Requirements

What You'll Own


Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone


Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)


Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them


Who You Are

AI-native. You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer. You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp. Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation. You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel. You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient. Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority. PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.

This Role Is NOT
